title: The Property-s Elements of a Skew Brace
statement: Let $B=(B,+,\circ)$ be a skew brace, write $a*b=-a+a\circ b-b$, and for $x\in B$ set $$\operatorname{Fix}^r(x)=\{b\in B:x*b=0\},\qquad \operatorname{Fix}^l(x)=\{b\in B:b*x=0\}.$$ If $C_x^+$ and $C_x^\circ$ are the centralizers of $x$ in $(B,+)$ and $(B,\circ)$, respectively, call $x$ an element with property $(s)$ when both indices $$[(B,+):\operatorname{Fix}^r(x)\cap C_x^+]\quad\text{and}\quad[(B,\circ):\operatorname{Fix}^l(x)\cap C_x^\circ]$$ are finite. Do the elements with property $(s)$ form an ideal of $B$?

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-22)

**Status:** open

**Assessment.** The property-(s) elements form an ideal for two-sided skew braces of abelian type, but the general question whether they form an ideal remains open in the latest primary treatment.
